source_text: Ὁ μὲν οὖν Ἰησοῦς ἐπιστρέφων τοὺς μαθητὰς οὐχὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ [μὴ] προσέχειν ἁπαξαπλῶς γόησι καὶ τοῖς ἐπαγγελλομένοις δι᾿ οἱασδήποτε ὁδοῦ ποιεῖν τεράστια (οὐ γὰρ ἐδέοντο τούτου οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ) ἀλλ᾿ ἀπὸ τοῦ τοῖς ἀναγορεύουσιν ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πειρωμένοις διά τινων φαντασιῶν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιστρέφειν τοὺς Ἰησοῦ μαθητὰς ὅπου μὲν εἶπε· „τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· ἰδοὺ ὧδε ὁ Χριστὸς ἢ ὧδε, μὴ πιστεύετε. ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ δώσουσι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα μεγάλα. ὥστε πλανᾶσθαι εἰ δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς. ἰδοὺ προείρηκα ὑμῖν. ἐὰν οὖν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν· ἰδοὺ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐστὶ, μὴ ἐξέλθητε· ἰδοὺ ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις, μὴ πιστεύσητε. ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἐξέρχεται ἀπ᾿ ἀνατολῶν καὶ φαίνεται ἕως δυσμῶν, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου“· ὅπου δέ· „πολλοὶ ἐροῦσί μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· κύριε, κύριε, οὐ τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐφάγομεν καὶ τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐπίομεν καὶ τῷ ὀνόματί σου δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν καὶ δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν; καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτοῖς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ. ὅτι ἐστὲ ἐργάται ἀδικίας.“ ὁ δὲ Κέλσος κοινοποιῆσαι βουλόμενος τὰ τεράστια τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς τὴν ἐν ἀνθρώποις γοητείαν φησὶν αὐταῖς λέξεσιν· ὦ φῶς καὶ ἀλήθεια, τῇ αὐτοῦ φωνῇ διαῤῥήδην ἐξαγορεύει, καθὰ καὶ ὑμεῖς συγγεγράφατε, διότι παρέσονται ὑμῖν καὶ ἕτεροι δυνάμεσιν ὁμοίαις χρώμενοι, κακοὶ καὶ γόητες, καὶ σατανᾶν τινα τοιαῦτα παραμηχανώμενον ὀνομάζει· ᾥστ᾿ οὐδὲ αὐτὸς ἔξαρνός ἐστιν, ὡς ταῦτά γε οὐδὲν θεῖον ἀλλὰ πονηρῶν ἐστιν ἔργα. βιαζόμενος δὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας ὁμοῦ καὶ τὰ τῶν ἄλλων ἀπεκάλυψε καὶ τὰ καθ᾿ αὑτὸν ἤλεγξε. πῶς οὖν οὐ σχέτλιον ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν ἔργων τὸν μὲν θεὸν τοὺς δὲ γόητας ἡγεῖσθαι; τί γὰρ μᾶλλον ἀπό γε τούτων τοὺς ἄλλους πονηροὺς ἢ τοῦτον νομιστέον αὐτῷ χρωμένους μάρτυρι; ταῦτα μέν γε καὶ αὐτὸς ὡμολόγησεν οὐχὶ θείας φύσεως ἀλλ᾿ ἀπατεώνων τινῶν καὶ παμπονήρων εἶναι γνωρίσματα. ὅρα δὴ εἰ μὴ ἐν τούτοις σαφῶς ὁ Κέλσος ἐλέγχεται κακουργῶν τὸν λόγον, ἄλλο μὲν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντος περὶ τῶν ποιησόντων „σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα,“ ἄλλο δὲ τοῦ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαίου φάσκοντος. καὶ γὰρ εἰ μὲν ἁπλῶς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἔλεγεν Ἰησοῦς φυλάσσεσθαι τοὺς τὰ τεράστια ἐπαγγελλομένους οὐ παρατιθέμενος, τί φήσουσιν ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι, τάχα χώραν εἶχεν ἂν ἡ ὑπόνοια αὐτοῦ· ἐπεὶ δ᾿ ἀφ᾿ ὧν θέλει ἡμᾶς φυλάσσεσθαι ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπαγγέλλονται εἶναι „ὁ Χριστὸς,“ ὅπερ οὐ ποιοῦσιν οἱ γόητες, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ βιοῦντας κακῶς φησι τινὰς δυνάμεις ποιήσειν καὶ δαίμονας ἀποβαλεῖν ἀνθρώπων· μᾶλλον δ᾿, εἰ δεῖ οὕτως εἰπεῖν, ἀποκηρύσσεται μὲν τῶν κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἡ γοητεία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ κατ᾿ αὐτῶν ὑπόνοια, εἰσάγεται δὲ ἡ θειότης τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θειότης τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δυνατόν τινα τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ χρησάμενον καὶ οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως ἐνεργηθέντα ὑπό τινος δυνάμεως πρὸς τὸ προσποιήσασθαι, ὅτι αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ Χριστὸς, δοκεῖν τὰ παραπλήσια ἐπιτελεῖν τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ ἄλλους τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τὰ ὡσπερεὶ παραπλήσια τοῖς γνησίοις αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς.
pass_a_gloss: Jesus, then, turning (ἐπιστρέφω) the disciples not from heeding (προσέχω) sorcerers (γόης) simply and those promising (ἐπαγγέλλομαι) by whatever way (ὁδός) to do wonders (τεράστια) (for his disciples did not need this), but from those proclaiming (ἀναγορεύω) themselves to be the Christ of God and trying through certain apparitions/illusions (φαντασίαι) to turn to themselves the disciples of Jesus, in one place said: 'then if anyone says to you, behold here the Christ or here, do not believe (πιστεύω); for false-christs (ψευδόχριστοι) and false-prophets (ψευδοπροφῆται) will be raised and will give signs (σημεῖα) and great wonders (τέρατα), so as to lead astray (πλανάω) if possible even the elect (ἐκλεκτοί). Behold I have foretold (προλέγω) you. If then they say to you, behold he is in the desert (ἔρημος), do not go out; behold in the inner rooms (ταμεῖα), do not believe. For as the lightning (ἀστραπή) comes out from the east (ἀνατολαί) and appears as far as the west (δυσμαί), so will be the coming (παρουσία) of the Son of Man'; and in another: 'many will say to me in that day: Lord, Lord (κύριε), did we not in your name (ὄνομα) eat and in your name drink and in your name cast out (ἐκβάλλω) demons (δαιμόνια) and do many powers (δυνάμεις)? And I will say to them: depart (ἀποχωρέω) from me, because you are workers of unrighteousness (ἐργάται ἀδικίας).' But Celsus, wishing to make common (κοινοποιέω) the wonders of Jesus with the sorcery among men, says in these very words (αὐταῖς λέξεσιν): 'O light and truth (φῶς καὶ ἀλήθεια)! With his own voice he expressly (διαρρήδην) declares (ἐξαγορεύω), just as you too have written down (συγγράφω), that there will come to you also others using similar powers, evil men (κακοί) and sorcerers, and he names a certain Satan (σατανᾶς) contriving (παραμηχανάομαι) such things; so that not even he himself is denying (ἔξαρνος) that these are nothing divine (θεῖον) but are works (ἔργα) of wicked men (πονηροί). But forced (βιάζομαι) by the truth he at once both uncovered (ἀποκαλύπτω) the [deeds] of the others and convicted (ἐλέγχω) his own. How then is it not wretched (σχέτλιος) from the same works to consider (ἡγέομαι) the one a god (θεός), the others sorcerers? For why rather, from these at least, must the others be thought wicked than this man, using him as witness (μάρτυς)? These things indeed he himself confessed (ὁμολογέω) to be marks (γνωρίσματα) not of a divine nature (θεία φύσις) but of certain deceivers (ἀπατεών) and utterly wicked (παμπόνηρος).' See (ὁράω) then whether in these Celsus is not clearly convicted of doing mischief to (κακουργέω) the argument, Jesus saying one thing about those who will do 'signs and wonders', and the Jew in Celsus claiming (φάσκω) another. For if Jesus simply told the disciples to guard against (φυλάσσομαι) those promising wonders, not setting out what they will say themselves to be, perhaps his suspicion (ὑπόνοια) would have had room (χώρα); but since those from whom Jesus wants us to guard ourselves profess to be 'the Christ', which sorcerers do not do, and he says that some living (βιόω) badly in the name of Jesus will do certain powers and cast demons out of men; rather, if one must say it so, there is disowned (ἀποκηρύσσω) from those [in] the passage (τόπος) sorcery and all the suspicion against them, and there is introduced (εἰσάγω) the divinity (θειότης) of Christ and divinity of his disciples, because it is possible that someone using his name and I know not how energized (ἐνεργέω) by some power to pretend (προσποιέομαι) that he himself is the Christ should seem (δοκέω) to accomplish (ἐπιτελέω) things similar (παραπλήσια) to Christ, and others in the name of Jesus things as it were similar to his genuine (γνήσιος) disciples.
pass_b_english: Jesus, then, was turning his disciples away, not from heeding sorcerers in general and those who promise to work wonders by any means whatever (for his disciples had no need of that), but from those who proclaim themselves to be the Christ of God and try, by certain illusions, to turn the disciples of Jesus to themselves, when he said in one place: “Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ,’ or ‘Here he is,’ do not believe it. For false christs and false prophets will arise and will perform great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect. See, I have told you beforehand. So if they say to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it. For as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man” (Matthew 24:23–27). And in another place: “Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not eat in your name, and drink in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works?’ And I will say to them, ‘Depart from me, for you are workers of unrighteousness’” (Matthew 7:22–23; Luke 13:26–27).

But Celsus, wishing to put the wonders of Jesus on a level with the sorcery found among men, says in these very words: “O light and truth! With his own voice he openly declares, as you yourselves have written, that others also will come to you using similar powers, wicked men and sorcerers; and he names a certain Satan who contrives such things. So not even he denies that these works are nothing divine but are the deeds of wicked men. Yet, constrained by the truth, he has at once exposed what the others do and convicted what he himself does. How then is it not monstrous, from the same works, to consider the one a god and the others sorcerers? For why, on the strength of these works at least, should we think the others wicked any more than this man, when we have him as our witness? He himself, indeed, admitted that these things are the marks not of a divine nature but of certain deceivers and utter scoundrels.”

See, then, whether in these words Celsus is not plainly caught maliciously twisting the argument, since Jesus says one thing about those who will perform “signs and wonders” (Matthew 24:24), and the Jew in Celsus claims another. If Jesus had simply told his disciples to beware of those who promise wonders, without setting out what they would claim to be, Celsus’s suspicion might perhaps have had some ground. But those against whom Jesus wants us to be on guard profess to be “the Christ” (Matthew 24:23), which sorcerers do not do; and he says further that some who live wickedly will do certain mighty works in the name of Jesus and cast demons out of people (Matthew 7:22). Rather, if one may put it this way, sorcery is banished from the matters in this passage, and so is every suspicion raised against them; and what is brought in is the divinity of Christ and the divinity of his disciples. For it is possible that someone who uses his name and, I do not know how, is moved by some power to pretend that he himself is the Christ, may seem to accomplish things like those of Christ; and that others, in the name of Jesus, may seem to accomplish things somewhat like those of his genuine disciples.

choices.why: ἐπιστρέφων (participle): removed added 'wished to'; recast as 'was turning his disciples away ... when he said in one place'
ταῦτα μέν γε: 'For he himself admitted' -> 'He himself, indeed, admitted' (no 'for' in Greek)
ἡ ὑπόνοια αὐτοῦ: 'his suspicion' (read as Jesus') -> 'Celsus's suspicion'
πᾶσα ἡ κατ' αὐτῶν ὑπόνοια: 'every suspicion of it' -> 'every suspicion raised against them'; τῶν κατὰ τὸν τόπον -> 'the matters in this passage'

translator_notes: Koetschau brackets [μὴ] in the first sentence as an intrusion; translated without it (‘not from heeding sorcerers’). Matthew 24:23-27 is quoted almost verbatim (Origen has πιστεύετε for πιστεύσητε in 24:23 and the order σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα μεγάλα). The second quotation blends Matthew 7:22-23 with Luke 13:26-27: ‘eat and drink’ comes from Luke 13:26 (there ‘in your presence’), and ‘workers of unrighteousness’ (ἐργάται ἀδικίας) from Luke 13:27; Matthew has ‘you who work lawlessness’. Both cited. Celsus’s quotation runs from ‘O light and truth’ to ‘utter scoundrels’ (Koetschau’s fragment). θεός of Jesus in Celsus’s mouth is lowercase ‘a god’ (sceptical voice). ‘A certain Satan’ keeps Celsus’s dismissive τινα. ἀποκηρύσσεται μὲν τῶν κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἡ γοητεία: literally ‘sorcery is disowned from those in the passage’; rendered ‘banished from the people this passage describes’ (the genitive could also be neuter, ‘from what the passage treats’; sense unchanged). Allusions back to the quoted texts are cited again inline (Matthew 24:23, 24; 7:22). Reviewer: ἡ ὑπόνοια αὐτοῦ is Celsus’s (or his Jew’s) suspicion, not Jesus’; named as Celsus’s to avoid the wrong referent. κατ’ αὐτῶν ὑπόνοια = suspicion against them (the matters of the passage), not ‘suspicion of it’.
